verdict.headline: Iran sanctions land milder than feared as Brent retreats ahead of Nvidia's print tomorrow
verdict.label: Brent $92.16 after 'Operation Economic Outcast'; 30Y 5.236%; S&P futures +0.12%; NVDA T-1 to Wednesday AH
verdict.rationale_short: The session's dominant macro risk — that Bessent's Iran press conference would push Brent above $94 and re-activate the regime trigger before NVDA's print — has resolved in the market's favor. 'Operation Economic Outcast' targeted ~60 Iranian entities with secondary sanctions on aviation, digital assets, gold, shipping, and technology, but stopped short of the blanket dollar-system exclusion oil traders had feared. Brent dropped to $92.16 from Monday's $93.16, now $1.84 below the $94 threshold. The 30Y also retreated to 5.236%, 6bps from the 5.30% trigger. Both regime indicators are moving away from thresholds entering NVDA's Wednesday AH print. Consumer Confidence (August) and Case-Shiller Home Price Index (June) at 10 AM ET are the session's remaining macro disruptors. The read changes if: (1) consumer confidence collapses below 85, signaling tariff-season household deterioration 22 days before the September FOMC; (2) AMD closes below $450 today — demand-skeptical chip-sector confirmation the session before the highest-bar print of the AI cycle; or (3) Warsh drops hawkish language from Jackson Hole before Friday that reverses the 30Y rally.

trade_setups.asset: Brent ($92.16) — Operation Economic Outcast resolved softer than feared; monitoring re-escalation
trade_setups.thesis: The morning's dominant macro risk — that Bessent's Iran press conference would push Brent above $94 and re-activate the regime trigger before NVDA's print — resolved in the market's favor. 'Operation Economic Outcast' was comprehensive in scope (~60 entities, 5 Iranian sectors) but stopped short of the blanket dollar-exclusion threat oil markets had priced. Brent dropped to $92.16, now $1.84 below the regime trigger. The regime trigger requires Brent above $94 AND 30Y above 5.30% simultaneously — both are retreating. The risk is re-escalation: Tehran has telegraphed Hormuz ship seizure threats, and a confirmed seizure would be a step-change escalation Brent hasn't priced.
trade_setups.entry: $94 close remains the regime re-trigger level. A reversal above $93.50 today on new Bessent follow-on language or a confirmed Hormuz seizure would narrow the gap materially. Current trajectory argues the worst-case scenario has been priced out for this week.
trade_setups.invalidation: Brent closes above $94 — regime trigger reactivated before NVDA's print. Or: Iran executes Hormuz vessel seizure; Brent could gap above $95.
trade_setups.horizon: 1 session (today's close); NVDA Wednesday AH print then resets the risk framework

trade_setups.asset: NVDA (~$215–$217) — T-1 holding pattern; macro improved but bar unchanged
trade_setups.thesis: NVDA enters T-1 with a better macro backdrop than Monday (Brent at $92.16 vs. $93.16, 30Y at 5.236% vs. 5.28% Friday) but faces the identical execution bar: consensus at $92B revenue and $2.09 EPS sits only 0.9% above the company's $91.0B guidance midpoint. The multiple (~22x forward revenue) compresses unless gross margin AND Q3 data-center guide simultaneously exceed the highest sell-side estimates. Today's session is a holding pattern — AMD's close and Consumer Confidence at 10 AM are the session's reads. The print tomorrow defines the setup.
trade_setups.entry: Below $210 before the print without a macro catalyst = demand-skeptical positioning, not a trading entry. Constructive resolution requires GM above 78% AND Q3 DC guide above ~$39B simultaneously on Wednesday.
trade_setups.invalidation: NVDA breaks below $210 intraday on no news — pre-print positioning unwinding. Or: Consumer Confidence collapse below 85 at 10 AM creates a macro-negative backdrop that compresses the multiple before the print.

trade_setups.asset: Consumer Confidence (Aug) + Case-Shiller (June) at 10 AM ET — session's only remaining macro disruptor
trade_setups.thesis: The July reading already fell to 90.8 (from 92.2 in June, missing expectations). The August reading arrives 22 days before the September 16 FOMC with US-Canada 50% tariffs live (effective Monday) and Canada retaliatory tariffs hitting dairy, appliances, and electronics September 8. A second consecutive miss — especially below 88 — would be the first data signal that US households are absorbing tariff-season cost-push faster than the soft-landing consensus expects. September FOMC hike odds currently at 30.6%; a consumer confidence collapse and Warsh-hawkish Jackson Hole keynote Friday is the path above 40%.
trade_setups.entry: Consumer Confidence below 85 = soft-landing crack signal; watch 30Y response — if 30Y re-crosses 5.26% on the print, the Warsh Friday keynote becomes the regime-watch event. Above 93 = consumer resilient; 30Y stays in 5.20–5.30% range and NVDA heads into Wednesday with a clean macro backdrop.
trade_setups.invalidation: Warsh makes market-moving comments at Jackson Hole before Friday's keynote (impromptu interview, panel remarks) that overshadow the data releases.
trade_setups.horizon: 10 AM ET release; September 16 FOMC is the medium-term context

bear_case: The morning's constructive read rests on two regime indicators simultaneously retreating — both can reverse. The operative bear sequence for the next 48 hours: Consumer Confidence at 10 AM ET collapses to or below 85, the first genuine signal that US consumers are absorbing the Canada 50% tariff cost-push ahead of Canada's September 8 retaliatory salvo. That reading arrives 22 days before the September FOMC and would push September hike odds from 30.6% toward 40%+, giving Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote Friday a hawkish backdrop that sends the 30Y through 5.30%. Simultaneously: AMD closes below $450 today — confirming demand-skeptical chip positioning after 10 consecutive sessions below $484 — entering NVDA's print without the leading indicator. Tomorrow, NVDA meets consensus ($92B revenue) without simultaneously exceeding both gross margin (above 78%) and Q3 DC guide (above ~$39B) thresholds — the most likely outcome given NVDA has fallen after 5 of the last 6 reports on beats of comparable magnitude. The resulting chip-sector selloff (-3-5% NVDA, AMD back toward $430) in a backdrop where the September FOMC just went 'live' and Warsh has yet to give Friday's keynote defines the maximum adverse entry point for the September FOMC window. Add an Iran re-escalation (Hormuz seizure, Brent back above $94) and the setup becomes the triple-overlay worst case: energy inflation re-ignites, long-end rates surge, and the highest-bar AI print of the cycle disappoints.
